papers.title: All Languages Matter: On the Multilingual Safety of Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Safety lies at the core of developing and deploying large language models (LLMs). However, previous safety benchmarks only concern the safety in one language, e.g. the majority language in the pretraining data such as English. In this work, we build the first multilingual safety benchmark for LLMs, XSafety, in response to the global deployment of LLMs in practice. XSafety covers 14 kinds of commonly used safety issues across 10 languages that span several language families. We utilize XSafety to empirically study the multilingual safety for 4 widely-used LLMs, including both close-API and open-source models. Experimental results show that all LLMs produce significantly more unsafe responses for non-English queries than English ones, indicating the necessity of developing safety alignment for non-English languages. In addition, we propose several simple and effective prompting methods to improve the multilingual safety of ChatGPT by evoking safety knowledge and improving cross-lingual generalization of safety alignment. Our prompting method can significantly reduce the ratio of unsafe responses from 19.1% to 9.7% for non-English queries. We release our data at https://github.com/Jarviswang94/Multilingual_safety_benchmark.

papers.title: Safety Assessment of Chinese Large Language Models
papers.abstract: With the rapid popularity of large language models such as ChatGPT and GPT-4, a growing amount of attention is paid to their safety concerns. These models may generate insulting and discriminatory content, reflect incorrect social values, and may be used for malicious purposes such as fraud and dissemination of misleading information. Evaluating and enhancing their safety is particularly essential for the wide application of large language models (LLMs). To further promote the safe deployment of LLMs, we develop a Chinese LLM safety assessment benchmark. Our benchmark explores the comprehensive safety performance of LLMs from two perspectives: 8 kinds of typical safety scenarios and 6 types of more challenging instruction attacks. Our benchmark is based on a straightforward process in which it provides the test prompts and evaluates the safety of the generated responses from the evaluated model. In evaluation, we utilize the LLM's strong evaluation ability and develop it as a safety evaluator by prompting. On top of this benchmark, we conduct safety assessments and analyze 15 LLMs including the OpenAI GPT series and other well-known Chinese LLMs, where we observe some interesting findings. For example, we find that instruction attacks are more likely to expose safety issues of all LLMs. Moreover, to promote the development and deployment of safe, responsible, and ethical AI, we publicly release SafetyPrompts including 100k augmented prompts and responses by LLMs.

papers.title: Safety at Scale: A Comprehensive Survey of Large Model and Agent Safety
papers.abstract: The rapid advancement of large models, driven by their exceptional abilities in learning and generalization through large-scale pre-training, has reshaped the landscape of Artificial Intelligence (AI). These models are now foundational to a wide range of applications, including conversational AI, recommendation systems, autonomous driving, content generation, medical diagnostics, and scientific discovery. However, their widespread deployment also exposes them to significant safety risks, raising concerns about robustness, reliability, and ethical implications. This survey provides a systematic review of current safety research on large models, covering Vision Foundation Models (VFMs), Large Language Models (LLMs), Vision-Language Pre-training (VLP) models, Vision-Language Models (VLMs), Diffusion Models (DMs), and large-model-powered Agents. Our contributions are summarized as follows: (1) We present a comprehensive taxonomy of safety threats to these models, including adversarial attacks, data poisoning, backdoor attacks, jailbreak and prompt injection attacks, energy-latency attacks, data and model extraction attacks, and emerging agent-specific threats. (2) We review defense strategies proposed for each type of attacks if available and summarize the commonly used datasets and benchmarks for safety research. (3) Building on this, we identify and discuss the open challenges in large model safety, emphasizing the need for comprehensive safety evaluations, scalable and effective defense mechanisms, and sustainable data practices. More importantly, we highlight the necessity of collective efforts from the research community and international collaboration. Our work can serve as a useful reference for researchers and practitioners, fostering the ongoing development of comprehensive defense systems and platforms to safeguard AI models.

papers.title: Enhanced Diagnostic and Interpretable Model for Febrile Diseases Using Explainable AI and Large Language Model
papers.abstract: <p><span>Tropical febrile diseases pose significant public health challenges in tropical regions, particularly in resource-limited settings, where timely and accurate diagnoses are critical for effective disease management. However, existing diagnostic systems are black-box and often lack interpretability, making it difficult for healthcare practitioners to understand and trust machine learning (ML) predictions. Additionally, the existing system excludes younger patients, limiting its applicability. This study aimed to develop an integrated diagnostic system that enhances interpretability by leveraging machine learning (ML), Explainable AI (XAI), and a large language model (LLM). A dataset comprising 3,914 patient records with 32 symptoms was obtained from a New Frontiers in Research Fund-sponsored project and preprocessed for analysis. Random Forest (RF) was trained with hyperparameter tuning using GridSearchCV and evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation to optimize its performance. The tuned model achieved high diagnostic performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in diagnosing six febrile diseases. To enhance interpretability, a Model Interpretability Framework (MIF) was incorporated, integrating Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) for visual insights and ChatGPT for textual explanations. This combination provided users with a clear understanding of the diagnostic process, addressing the limitations of black-box ML models. The system was implemented using Python in a development environment that included Google Colaboratory, Visual Studio Code, Flet, and MySQL for database management. Agile development methodology and Unified Modeling Language tools were employed to create a user-friendly design for clinicians and patients. The diagnostic system was evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC metrics. The RF model achieved outstanding precision for most diseases, high recall (≥0.97), and an AUC-ROC of 0.99, indicating nearly flawless training performance with few misclassifications. On the test dataset, the model performed better in diagnosing malaria (F1-score = 88%, precision = 85%), urinary tract infection (F1-score = 72%, precision = 80%), and respiratory tract infection (F1-score = 72%, precision = 77%). The evaluated system demonstrated strong predictive performance, correctly identifying 72 out of 99 tested patient cases, with 26 cases misclassified and one case completely missed. It achieved the highest detection rates for Malaria and HIV/AIDS, accurately identifying all cases without false positives. This work enhances diagnostic solutions for tropical healthcare settings by improving explainability and ensuring inclusivity for younger patients, addressing key limitations in existing systems. The integration of ML, XAI, and LLM enhances diagnostic performance and lays the groundwork for future AI-driven healthcare innovations, ultimately improving health outcomes in resource-scarce regions. Healthcare providers should adopt this system to enhance the efficiency of disease diagnosis and extend the system to diagnose additional medical conditions.&nbsp;</span></p>

literature_themes.theme: Safety Assessment of Large Language Models Across Languages
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers focuses on the safety evaluation of large language models (LLMs) in multilingual contexts. It introduces benchmarks for assessing safety across multiple languages, particularly highlighting the disparities in safety performance between English and non-English queries. The studies reveal that LLMs tend to produce more unsafe responses for non-English inputs and propose methods to enhance safety through effective prompting techniques. Additionally, a comprehensive survey outlines various safety threats and defense mechanisms associated with large models.
literature_themes.limitations: The studies primarily emphasize the safety of LLMs in specific languages, such as English and Chinese, which may overlook safety issues in other languages. Moreover, while benchmarks are proposed, the effectiveness of the suggested prompting methods may vary across different contexts and models, and there is a lack of longitudinal studies to assess the long-term safety implications of LLM deployment.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies a significant research gap in the multilingual safety of LLMs, particularly in non-English contexts. It underscores the need for developing robust safety frameworks that can be generalized across diverse languages and cultural contexts, paving the way for future research on inclusive and comprehensive safety assessments in AI.

literature_themes.theme: Enhancing Few-Shot Recommender Systems with Language Models
literature_themes.summary: This cluster investigates the integration of large language models to improve the representation capabilities of few-shot recommender systems, aiming to enhance their performance in scenarios with limited data.
literature_themes.limitations: The cluster lacks comprehensive empirical evaluations across diverse datasets and does not address the computational overhead introduced by large language models in real-time recommendation scenarios.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the potential for further research in optimizing few-shot learning techniques and exploring the trade-offs between model complexity and recommendation accuracy, identifying gaps in current methodologies.

summary: Recent studies emphasize the importance of interpretable internal representations in large language models to improve safety and controllability. Techniques such as attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation are explored to enhance understanding of model decisions. These approaches aim to mitigate risks associated with model unpredictability and ensure alignment with human values, ultimately fostering trust in AI systems.
scholarly_positioning: While existing approaches, such as attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation, have made strides in interpreting internal representations of large language models, they often fall short in providing comprehensive insights into model decision-making processes. These methods may not fully address the inherent unpredictability of these models, leaving significant gaps in safety and controllability. Furthermore, the alignment of model outputs with human values remains a critical challenge that has not been adequately resolved. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing novel techniques that enhance interpretability, thereby fostering greater trust and ensuring that large language models operate within acceptable safety parameters.
research_scope: This study will focus on enhancing the interpretability of internal representations in large language models (LLMs) used for automated customer service chatbots in the retail sector. The research will involve a comparative analysis of existing interpretability techniques, such as attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation, against a novel interpretability framework developed by the researcher. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the performance of the chatbots will be assessed using user satisfaction surveys and error rate tracking as primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes will include the alignment of chatbot responses with predefined human values and the frequency of model misinterpretations. The study aims to provide insights into improving safety and controllability in LLMs deployed in customer service applications.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated that techniques like attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation enhance interpretability in large language models (LLMs) used in automated customer service; however, they treat the alignment of model outputs with human values as secondary, leaving unclear whether these interpretability techniques effectively improve user satisfaction and reduce misinterpretations. This matters practically because ensuring that LLMs operate within acceptable safety parameters is crucial for fostering trust in AI systems. Therefore, this study investigates the effectiveness of a novel interpretability framework in enhancing both user satisfaction and alignment with human values in customer service chatbots.
question: How does the implementation of a novel interpretability framework, compared to traditional techniques like attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation, affect user satisfaction and the alignment of responses with human values in automated customer service chatbots within the retail sector?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the impact of a novel interpretability framework (independent variable) on user satisfaction and alignment with human values (dependent variables) in automated customer service chatbots. The framework enhances the interpretability of internal representations, serving as a mediator that improves users' understanding of model decisions. This understanding influences user trust and satisfaction, leading to better alignment of chatbot responses with human values. The theoretical framework is grounded in cognitive psychology, suggesting that clearer interpretability reduces cognitive load and misinterpretations, thereby enhancing user experience. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include that increased interpretability directly correlates with user satisfaction and that improved satisfaction leads to better alignment with human values.
hypothesis: The implementation of a novel interpretability framework in automated customer service chatbots will lead to higher user satisfaction compared to traditional techniques like attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation, with increased interpretability serving as a mediator that enhances this effect.
operationalization_causal_check:
Construct Operationalization Table:

| Construct Name                     | Role       | Measurement Instrument       | Data Source                     | Timing          |
|------------------------------------|------------|------------------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------|
| Novel Interpretability Framework    | IV         | Framework Evaluation Metrics | Chatbot System Logs             | Pre and Post-Implementation |
| User Satisfaction                   | DV         | User Satisfaction Surveys    | User Feedback                    | After Interaction  |
| Alignment with Human Values         | DV         | Value Alignment Assessment   | Expert Review of Chatbot Outputs | After Interaction  |
| Interpretability                    | Mediator   | Interpretability Scores      | User Feedback and System Logs    | During Interaction |

Causal Pathway: The implementation of the novel interpretability framework (IV) is expected to enhance interpretability (mediator), which in turn is hypothesized to increase user satisfaction (DV) and improve alignment with human values (DV). 

Likely Confounds: User demographics, prior experience with chatbots, and individual differences in cognitive load may influence user satisfaction and perceived alignment with human values. 

Claim Boundaries: The study can claim that the novel interpretability framework enhances user satisfaction and alignment with human values compared to traditional methods, but cannot definitively establish causation without controlling for confounding variables. 

What Cannot Be Concluded: The study cannot conclude that the novel framework is the only factor influencing user satisfaction and alignment; other external factors may also play a significant role.
methodology: This study will employ a three-arm design involving a novel interpretability framework as the target intervention, traditional techniques (attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation) as the active control, and a standard chatbot implementation as the usual-care baseline. Participants will be recruited from a retail customer service context, ensuring a diverse demographic representation. The procedure will involve deploying each chatbot version for user interactions over a six-month period, collecting data on user satisfaction through surveys and alignment with human values via expert reviews of chatbot outputs. Operationalized variables will include interpretability scores derived from user feedback and system logs, while evaluation metrics will focus on user satisfaction ratings and the frequency of misinterpretations. To control for confounding variables, participant demographics and prior chatbot experience will be recorded and analyzed. Statistical reasoning will involve ANOVA to compare group means, ensuring robust validity in findings and reproducibility through detailed documentation of the methodology and data collection processes.

proposal: This research proposes to enhance the interpretability of internal representations in large language models (LLMs) utilized in automated customer service chatbots within the retail sector, addressing the critical gap identified in existing literature regarding the insufficient focus on user satisfaction and alignment with human values. Prior studies, while exploring techniques like attention visualization and layer-wise relevance propagation, have not adequately linked interpretability improvements to tangible user outcomes, thus limiting their practical applicability. The central research question investigates how the implementation of a novel interpretability framework (independent variable) influences user satisfaction and alignment with human values (dependent variables) through enhanced interpretability as a mediator. The hypothesis posits that the novel framework will yield higher user satisfaction compared to traditional methods, with interpretability enhancing this effect. This study will employ a three-arm design, comparing the novel framework against traditional techniques and a standard chatbot implementation, with user satisfaction measured through validated surveys and alignment assessed via expert reviews of chatbot outputs. Operationalized constructs will include interpretability scores, user satisfaction ratings, and alignment metrics, while controlling for demographic variables and prior chatbot experience. The methodology will ensure robust validity through ANOVA analysis, with a focus on reproducibility and comprehensive data collection protocols. This research contributes theoretically by integrating cognitive psychology principles into interpretability, methodologically through a rigorous comparative design, and practically by providing actionable insights for improving user trust in AI systems. Key limitations include potential confounding variables and the challenge of ensuring diverse user engagement, which will be addressed through detailed participant recruitment and iterative feedback mechanisms.
